headline: Trump names his sixth press secretary
summary: Katie Zacharia, 42, a lawyer and TV commentator, is Trump's pick for White House press secretary, his sixth across two terms. Since June she has advised Trump Media, the company behind Truth Social. She spent two months this year as a Homeland Security spokesperson and left, she said, for her family. Karoline Leavitt left in August.
cover_answer: The president's helper who answers reporters' questions.
table_question: Is a loyal friend or an honest one the better messenger?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president picked a new helper to answer reporters' questions every day. Her name is Katie Zacharia, she is a lawyer, and she has four kids. It is like being the one friend who tells the whole class what the coach said. Nothing changes for you.
5-7.why: One helper, one job, four kids. The podium stays out of it.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script gives one person and one job: answering questions. Four kids is the detail they keep, and the friend relaying the coach is a picture from their own week. Expect "is she nice?" The articles don't say. She has four kids and talks on TV, and that is what we know.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Karoline Leavitt left the White House podium in August. Trump picked Katie Zacharia, a lawyer at his media company, as his sixth press secretary in two terms. The class rep who reads the teacher's rules to the room: the teacher wrote them, the rep takes the questions.
8-12.why: Someone left, someone was picked, sixth in the job.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect and whether rules get applied evenly, so the script runs one chain: Leavitt left, Trump picked Zacharia, she is the sixth. The class rep reading the rules is their mechanism. Expect "why so many?" Trump said Leavitt wanted time with her family. The articles don't say why the others left.

13-17.script: Should the president's spokesperson be paid by his company first? Katie Zacharia advises Trump's media company, and now takes the podium. Second: she called herself a "huge fan of ICE" on CNN. Is the job to inform you, or to win?
13-17.why: Inform or win. Let them pick a side, then switch.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: a press secretary works for the president, and the briefing room exists for the public. The script gives her employer and her own words and asks what the job is for. Argument is practised, so let them argue the White House's side first. Expect "aren't they all loyal?" Yes. Ask what it costs us.

5-7.a: The president's helper who stands at a desk and answers reporters' questions out loud, so everyone hears the same answer.

8-12.a: Six across two terms. Trump said Leavitt wanted time with her family. The articles don't say why the rest left.

8-12.q: Does she just say what he tells her?
8-12.a: The job is to explain his decisions and take the questions. The BBC says she has defended him on TV for years.

13-17.a: The public, once she starts. Until now Trump's media company paid her as an adviser.
No. A lawyer and a commentator on Fox News, CNN and Newsmax, arguing the president's side.
